name: Taj Mahal
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna river.
detailed_description: The Taj Mahal was commissioned in 1631 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal. It is regarded by many as the best example of Mughal architecture and a symbol of India's rich historical heritage, attracting millions of international and domestic visitors each year.
image_attribution: Photo via Unsplash / Wikimedia Commons License CC0/CC-BY-SA
entry_fee_info: INR 50 for Indian citizens, INR 1100 for foreign tourists (Verified ASI)
opening_hours_info: 30 minutes before sunrise to 30 minutes before sunset (Closed on Fridays)

name: Pangong Tso
short_description: Endorheic high-altitude saline lake in the Himalayas that changes colors from azure to indigo.
detailed_description: Pangong Tso extends from India to the Tibetan Autonomous Region. Situated at an altitude of 4,225 meters, this 134-kilometer-long lake is world-renowned for its crystalline waters that shift shades of blue, green, and turquoise throughout the daylight hours against barren arid mountain crags.
image_attribution: Photo via Unsplash / Open Tourism Archive
entry_fee_info: Inner Line Permit required (INR 400 + Wildlife fee)
opening_hours_info: Accessible during daylight hours in permitted months

name: Valley of Flowers National Park
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage high-altitude alpine meadow carpeted with endemic alpine flora.
detailed_description: Nested in the Western Himalayas of Chamoli district, Valley of Flowers National Park is renowned for its meadows of endemic alpine blossoms and diverse wildlife, including the snow leopard, Asiatic black bear, and blue sheep. The trek passes through the dramatic Pushpawati river gorge.
highlights: Over 500 species of wild flowering plants
image_attribution: Uttarakhand Forest Department & Public Domain Commons
entry_fee_info: INR 150 for Indian nationals, INR 600 for foreigners (valid for 3 days)
opening_hours_info: 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM (Last entry at 2:00 PM; camping not permitted)

name: Ranthambore National Park
short_description: Premier tiger reserve in Sawai Madhopur famous for Bengal tigers against 10th-century fortress ruins.
detailed_description: Ranthambore is one of the most prominent tiger habitats in northern India. Spread across dry deciduous forests and open grasslands, it offers exceptional opportunities to observe the Royal Bengal Tiger, leopards, marsh crocodiles, and sloth bears amidst historic stone ruins and scenic lakes.
image_attribution: Rajasthan Forest Department & Open Wildlife Media
entry_fee_info: Canter safari INR 850-1200, Gypsy safari INR 1800-2400 per person
opening_hours_info: Morning safari (6:30 AM to 10:00 AM), Evening safari (2:30 PM to 6:00 PM)

name: Varanasi Ghats & Kashi Vishwanath
short_description: Ancient sacred riverfront steps along the holy Ganges, known for mesmerizing evening Ganga Aarti.
detailed_description: Varanasi is among the world's oldest continually inhabited cities. Its 88 stone ghats along the crescent-shaped Ganges are epicenters of Hindu spirituality, morning classical ragas, vibrant boat processions, and the spellbinding Dashashwamedh Ghat Aarti.
image_attribution: Uttar Pradesh Tourism & Unsplash Free License
entry_fee_info: Ghats are free and open. Kashi Vishwanath corridor entry is free; special pooja options available
opening_hours_info: Ghats accessible 24 hours. Evening Aarti starts at sunset (around 6:30 PM)

name: Munnar Tea Highlands
short_description: Sprawling emerald tea plantations, mist-covered Western Ghats valleys, and Anamudi peak.
detailed_description: Perched at the confluence of three mountain streams in Kerala's Idukki district, Munnar is south India's premier hill station. Verdant tea estates carpet undulating hills, home to Eravikulam National Park and the endangered Nilgiri Tahr.
highlights: Anamudi - highest peak in South India
entry_fee_info: Tea Museum INR 125. Eravikulam Park INR 200
opening_hours_info: Eravikulam Park: 7:30 AM to 4:00 PM

name: Palolem Beach
short_description: Scenic crescent bay in South Goa bordered by lush coconut groves and tranquil warm waters.
detailed_description: Palolem is celebrated as one of Goa's most picturesque white-sand beaches. Sheltered between two rocky headlands in Canacona, its calm seas provide safe swimming, dolphin spotting cruises, and laid-back beachside bamboo shacks.
entry_fee_info: Free public beach access. Kayaks approx INR 300/hr
opening_hours_info: Open 24 hours daily. Lifeguards on duty 7:30 AM to 6:00 PM

name: Hampi Ruins & Monuments
short_description: Magnificent UNESCO World Heritage ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire amidst boulder-strewn terrain.
detailed_description: Hampi was the grand capital of the 14th-century Vijayanagara Empire. Situated along the Tungabhadra River, it showcases monumental Dravidian temples, the famed stone chariot of Vijaya Vittala, royal baths, and sprawling monolithic boulder formations.
image_attribution: Archaeological Survey of India & Creative Commons
entry_fee_info: INR 40 for Indians, INR 600 for foreign tourists (Vittala & Zenana enclosure)
opening_hours_info: 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM daily

name: Kaziranga National Park
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage floodplains sheltering two-thirds of the world's great one-horned rhinoceroses.
detailed_description: Located in Assam's Golaghat and Nagaon districts along the Brahmaputra River, Kaziranga features dense tall elephant grass, marshlands, and tropical broadleaf forests. It hosts significant breeding populations of elephants, wild water buffalo, and swamp deer alongside the majestic rhinoceros.
entry_fee_info: INR 100 Indian entry + Jeep Safari fee (~INR 2000-3000 per vehicle)
opening_hours_info: Safaris operate from 7:30 AM to 10:00 AM and 1:30 PM to 3:30 PM

name: Jaipur City Palace & Hawa Mahal
short_description: The Pink City's royal seat blending Rajput, Mughal, and European palace architecture.
detailed_description: Jaipur, founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, is the capital of Rajasthan. The City Palace complex features vast courtyards, the Mubarak Mahal museum, and the Peacock Gate. Nearby stands the 5-story honeycomb facade of Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds).
entry_fee_info: INR 300 Indian, INR 700 Foreigner for Museum; royal suite tour separate
opening_hours_info: 9:30 AM to 5:00 PM; Night viewing 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM

name: Marine Drive Promenade
short_description: Iconic 3.6-kilometer C-shaped boulevard along the Arabian Sea known as the Queen's Necklace.
detailed_description: Marine Drive is a grand arc of coastal promenade in South Mumbai. Known for its Art Deco buildings—recognized as part of a UNESCO World Heritage precinct—it is a beloved hub for evening breezes, sunset vistas, street snacks, and sparkling night views.
highlights: Arabian sea breezes and tetrapod breakers
entry_fee_info: Open public promenade with free access
opening_hours_info: Open 24 hours daily

name: Nohkalikai Falls & Cherrapunji
short_description: India's tallest plunge waterfall cascading 340 meters into an emerald pool amid mist-clad Khasi hills.
detailed_description: Located near Sohra (Cherrapunji) on the edge of the Meghalaya plateau, Nohkalikai Falls plunges dramatically off a forested sandstone precipice. The surrounding region is famous for living root bridges crafted by Khasi artisans and ancient limestone caves.
entry_fee_info: INR 50 per visitor at viewpoint
opening_hours_info: 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM daily

name: Manali & Solang Valley
short_description: Alpine resort town at the northern end of Kullu Valley, gateway to Rohtang Pass and adventure sports.
detailed_description: Framed by snow-clad Pir Panjal and Dhauladhar ranges, Manali is a hub for mountaineering, paragliding, skiing, and Himalayan treks. The scenic Solang Valley offers year-round outdoor sports and leads through the engineering marvel of Atal Tunnel towards Lahaul.
highlights: Old Manali apple orchards and cafes
entry_fee_info: Free town entry. Rohtang Pass green permit INR 550 per vehicle
opening_hours_info: Open year-round; Rohtang Pass subject to snow conditions (May-Nov)

name: Dal Lake & Srinagar Mughal Gardens
short_description: The Jewel of Srinagar featuring ornate wooden houseboats, floating flower markets, and Shikara rides.
detailed_description: Dal Lake is integral to Srinagar's cultural heritage. Encircled by the Zabarwan mountain range and Persian-style Mughal gardens (Shalimar Bagh and Nishat Bagh), the lake features floating vegetable markets, lotus blossoms, and intricately hand-carved cedar houseboats.
highlights: Shikara boat rides at golden hour
entry_fee_info: Mughal Gardens INR 24. Shikara ride regulated at INR 700-1000 per hour
opening_hours_info: Open daily; gardens open 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM

name: Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib)
short_description: Spiritual center of Sikhism, gilded in gold leaf and surrounded by the sacred Amrit Sarovar.
detailed_description: Sri Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar welcomes all individuals regardless of caste, faith, or nationality. It is famous for its shimmering gilded sanctum, serene sacred pool (Amrit Sarovar), and Guru-ka-Langar, the world's largest community kitchen serving over 100,000 free hot meals daily.
highlights: Golden sanctum reflection in Amrit Sarovar
image_attribution: Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee & Open Punjab Media
entry_fee_info: Free entry for all visitors. Free vegetarian meals at Langar
opening_hours_info: Open 24 hours every day of the year

name: Jim Corbett National Park
short_description: India's oldest national park in the Himalayan foothills along the Ramganga river.
detailed_description: Established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, Corbett spans 520 square kilometers of hills, marshy depressions, riverine belts, grasslands, and large lake reservoirs. It is home to tigers, wild Asiatic elephants, leopards, and over 580 species of resident and migratory birds.
highlights: Dense sal and teak Himalayan forests
entry_fee_info: Jeep permit from INR 4500 per vehicle (inclusive of guide and permit)
opening_hours_info: Dhikala zone open Nov 15 - June 15; Bijrani open Oct 15 - June 30

name: Qutub Minar & Mehrauli Archaeological Park
short_description: UNESCO World Heritage 72.5-meter red sandstone minaret and 4th-century rust-resistant Iron Pillar.
detailed_description: Commenced in 1192 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, the Qutub Minar is the world's tallest brick minaret. The complex includes the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, the intricately inscribed Alai Darwaza, and the famous ancient rust-resistant Iron Pillar of Chandragupta II.
image_attribution: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & Open Registry
entry_fee_info: INR 50 for Indians, INR 600 for foreign visitors (ASI cashless ticket)
opening_hours_info: 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily (illuminated at night)

name: Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Qila)
short_description: Living golden sandstone fortress rising from the dunes of the Thar Desert.
detailed_description: Built in 1156 AD by the Rajput ruler Rawal Jaisal, Sonar Qila (Golden Fort) is one of the world's very few living forts, housing roughly a quarter of the old city's population inside its triple-ringed ramparts. Within lie seven intricately carved Jain temples and ancient merchant havelis.
highlights: Sunset camel desert safari at Sam Dunes
entry_fee_info: Fort entrance is free. Fort Palace Museum INR 100 Indian, INR 500 Foreigner
opening_hours_info: Open 24 hours (Museum: 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM)

name: Radhanagar Beach (Beach No. 7)
short_description: Blue Flag certified white-sand shoreline on Havelock Island, consistently ranked among Asia's best.
detailed_description: Radhanagar Beach on Swaraj Dweep (Havelock) is famed for pristine powdery white sands, turquoise waters, and backdrop of primeval tropical rainforest. The beach is a protected eco-zone offering exceptional swimming and vivid crimson sunsets.
entry_fee_info: Free public beach entry. Island ferry tickets booked via DSS/private catamarans
opening_hours_info: 6:00 AM to 5:30 PM (swimming prohibited after sunset for safety)

name: Rishikesh & Ganga Riverfront
short_description: Yoga capital of the world and premier white-water rafting hub in the foothills of Garhwal.
detailed_description: Rishikesh sits where the holy Ganges emerges from the Himalayas onto the northern plains. Renowned globally for ashrams and yoga retreats, it is equally famed as an adventure sports capital for river rafting, bungee jumping, and cliff jumping.
highlights: White water rafting on the Ganges (Grades I-IV)
Ram Jhula and Lakshman Jhula suspension bridges
entry_fee_info: Ghats are free. Rafting packages range from INR 600 to INR 1500 per person
opening_hours_info: Open 24 hours. River activities operate sunrise to sunset
